D.t: Cory Booker leads by 24.9 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 890,850 votes; a one point swing is about 17,860 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +15.9 and D +34.4. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Essex, a projected net 169,419 votes; Hudson, a projected net 104,279 votes; Middlesex, a projected net 100,727 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Monmouth, D +11.7, 8.0% of the vote; Gloucester, D +8.6, 3.7% of the vote; Sussex, R +7.5, 1.8% of the vote; Hunterdon, D +10.7, 1.8% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Cory Booker runs furthest behind in Mercer, Burlington, Camden. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 69% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.43 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 57% of voters, 61 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.83 points; Voters without a degree, 51% of voters, 60 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.54 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Cory Booker: Immigration voters 30 to 67, Midsize counties 51 to 45, Incomes $125K and up 54 to 44. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
